attribution.note: Marcus states and endorses the proposition in his own words.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves the explicit requirement and present-tense assessment. The surrounding doubts about eventual success are separate from this observation.

contract.note: Reading this as a present assessment of agent reliability is ordinary and fair. Recent evaluations before publication reasonably test that reading, though they cannot establish that LLMs will never achieve reliability.

evidence.note: The May 2025 benchmark reports low overall and multi-turn success, plus confidentiality failures. Stronger performance in one workflow category does not establish broad reliability.
The dated version reports 30% autonomous completion in a simulated workplace and difficulty with longer tasks, supporting the present reliability assessment.
Improving task horizons challenge a no-progress interpretation, but do not demonstrate robust performance on realistic tasks as of the post. The study also reports limitations on messier tasks.

reviews.rationale: Contemporaneous benchmarks show substantial failures across realistic business and workplace tasks, supporting the contract's fair present-state reading. Workflow successes and METR's improving horizons qualify the picture without establishing broad trustworthy performance. This does not resolve eventual LLM capability.
